Legacy campaign

Everybody Plugs In (1942–1961)

More homes and businesses need electricity. Build enough room for growth before a busy grid becomes a fragile one.

Explore the Legacy campaign↗ See what’s at stake ↓

Build one utility across nine generations. This chapter is part of that journey.

Location
A fictional California utility
Starts in
1942
Generation
20 years

The situation

Your starting point

The fourth Legacy generation inherits a utility shaped by sixty years of earlier choices. Demand rises during your term as more electricity use puts the existing fleet to work.

A featured checkpoint asks for spare capacity relative to the opening peak. Meeting it means thinking ahead: a plant commissioned after the checkpoint will not help, however useful it becomes later.

The choices

What will you do?

  1. 01

    Build ahead of the busiest hours

    Watch the supply outlook as demand grows. Capacity that barely met the opening load may have little margin left when the checkpoint arrives.

  2. 02

    Keep expansion affordable

    Balance the cost of extra reserve with the campaign's customer-bill and debt objectives. Readiness is part of the service your utility sells.

  3. 03

    Prepare another handover

    Choose equipment with the next term in mind. New plants will age into your successor's fleet rather than disappear when your term ends.

Put your plan to the test

Continue the campaign and build a company with room for the next wave of electricity demand.

Open the campaign setup to begin, or continue your existing company. Later generations inherit the choices you made before them.
